newsitem.title: FRANCE: Parliament completes air liability first reading.
newsitem.headline: Parliament completes air liability first reading.

text.p: The European Parliament completed its first reading on Tuesday of the draft regulation on air carrier liability in the case of accidents.
The Strasbourg plenary adopted all 19 amendments related to the draft Council Regulation, COM(95)724, as proposed by Spanish rapporteur Isidoro Sanchez Garcia of the European Radical Alliance.

One of the amendments, if retained by the European Commission and the Council of Ministers, would raise the limit for carriers' objective liability compensation by 20,000 Ecus to 120,000 Ecus per passenger. Even if a carrier were to prove that it had taken all measures necessary to avoid damage it would continue to be held liable up to that limit.
European Commissioner Hans van den Broek, who attended the Monday debate on the proposal, was said by the parliament's Session News to have said the amendment was acceptable.

The Commission proposal sets out to abolish existing Warsaw Convention limits on air carrier liability; to lay down the principle of objective liability up to the sum of 100,000 Ecus; to set up a system of emergency payments for relatives of killed or injured passengers and; to allow victims or their relatives to bring liability court actions in their own countries.
The file, dealt with under the cooperation procedure, now returns to the Commission.
